title: What Separates Remote Work Winners from Remote Work Losers
author: Joel Trubman
summary: Trubman analyzes LSE research on 801 UK firms adapting to remote work post-2020 and identifies three enablers of success: early adoption (42% report positive impact vs. 7% for late adopters), systematic training (double the positive outcomes), and formal management practices (structured check-ins, adjusted KPIs, dashboards). The deeper lesson transcends remote work: managerial foresight and capability determine success in any change. At organizational scale, success flows from systematic alignment around strategy and clear management practices, not individual talent. Firms that allowed people to figure things out without training or oversight suffered; those that built good practices in advance succeeded. Trubman applies the same framework to AI adoption: companies moving early with structured training and clear management systems will outpace reactive late-adopters. The conclusion: CEOs who navigate change well have built operating models where foresight, training, and structured management are standard practice rather than crisis responses. Organizational quality at scale equals managerial quality.
points: Early movers on remote work adoption showed 6x better productivity outcomes than late adopters; timing matters because it allows time for systematic adaptation rather than crisis response.

Managerial foresight and capability is the core variable determining success in any organizational change; training and structured management practices scale productivity while ad-hoc adaptation produces suffering.

At scale, organizational quality is determined by managerial quality and systematic alignment around strategy, not individual heroics; good managers need clear KPIs, structured check-ins, and regular review.
Reactive adoption without training and structure is the path of suffering; proactive systems built in advance convert change from crisis to opportunity.
The three factors driving remote work success (early adoption, training, formal management practices) apply to AI adoption and any organizational change.
quotes: Companies that had introduced remote work before 2020 reported positive productivity impacts at 42%, compared to 7% for firms that adopted in 2022 or later. Jumping in early apparently really helped.
Training investment. Companies that trained staff systematically reported almost double the positive productivity outcomes from remote work compared to those with no training.

For any organization at scale, the quality of managers is the quality of the company. This is because past 50 or so employees, success is attained primarily through systematic alignment around a shared strategy.
The firms that let people figure stuff out on their own, with no training or oversight, and who only saw the future once it had already arrived — those were the ones who suffered.

The CEOs who navigate change well tend to have built an operating model that treats foresight, training, and structured management as standard practice rather than as responses to crisis.” Archived from Managing the Future Substack on May 3, 2026 by Tim.
